t: You're on Vanbrugh Hill, a street in the Royal Borough of Greenwich. It takes its name from Sir John Vanbrugh, an English architect and dramatist. He is perhaps best known for designing Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard. He also wrote two outspoken Restoration comedies, The Relapse and The Provoked Wife, which caused much controversy at first and remain favourites on the stage. He was knighted in 1714. The street is a quiet way to remember a man who worked in both architecture and the theatre.
